title: Autoscale Sentinel: adaptive target-curves and safety-fence tuning for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement an 'Autoscale Sentinel' policy engine that synthesizes multiple target metrics (tokens/sec, request concurrency, p50/p95 latency) into a single stability-aware scale intent, and apply configurable safety-fences to avoid oscillation or dangerous surges on Dedicated fleets. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a canary rollout for the policy runtime plug-in used by Dedicated capacity managers.

Background: Current autoscalers target single signals (typically throughput) and use fixed step/slew limits. We have seen two recurring failure modes on Dedicated pools: 1) overreaction to short-lived bursts causing expensive surge scaling, and 2) under-provisioning when token bursts coincide with KV-cache cold starts. The Sentinel policy should smooth noisy inputs, honor tenant throughput guarantees, and provide explicit 'credit' and 'fence' constructs for controlled bursts.

Scope of work:
- Define canonical target metrics and transformation curves (raw metric -> normalized score).
- Implement a curve-composer which weights metrics per-tenant and produces a composite scale score.
- Add algorithm variants: proportional-stepper, rate-of-change dampener (derivative), and credit-bank burst allowance.
- Safety fences: max_percent_scale_per_minute, minimum_headroom, cooldown_windows, and prewarm_window for KV-affinity.
- Telemetry: expose per-decision reasoning payloads (inputs, weights, resulting scale delta) in Console for audit and SLO debugging.
- E2E tests: replay historical production traces; synthetic stress with k6; chaos tests for controller restarts.

Non-goals: autoscaling cost-optimization heuristics (this belongs to Optimize), model variant fallbacks (separate ticket), or scheduler-level pod placement changes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical metric set defined and documented in Confluence with transformation functions
Curve-composer prototype implemented in policy-runtime library with unit tests
Three algorithm variants coded and feature-flagged: proportional-stepper, derivative-dampener, credit-bank
Safety fences configurable at fleet and tenant level and enforced in the runtime
Decision telemetry emitted to Console with <500ms latency overhead under 95th percentile load
Canary rollout (5% of fleets) completes 72h with no latency/SLO regressions; monitoring dashboards show expected behavior

testing_plan: Unit tests covering normalization, weighting, and scale delta calculations
Integration test in local dev cluster with a stubbed scheduler (run by CI)
Replay tests: run 30 days of sampled production traces through policy runtime and assert no >2x scale oscillation compared to baseline
Synthetic load: k6 scenarios to create short bursts and steady increases; verify credit-bank behavior and cooldowns
Chaos: controller restart during large burst to ensure idempotent reconcilation and no repeated scaling beyond fences
Safety sim: Monte Carlo variance analysis on metric noise to confirm fences limit cost exposure to configured thresholds
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal test clusters (dev, staging) for 2 weeks
Stage 2: Canary 5% of Dedicated fleets with strict observability and rollback alerting for 72h
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 30% after no regressions for 1 week, tune weights from observed telemetry
Stage 4: Full roll when KPIs stable for 14 days; ship release note and update runbooks
decisions: Normalization: use percentile clipping (5th-95th) + log-scale transform for token/sec to bound outliers
Composite scoring: weighted-sum with tenant-configurable weights; default favors p50 latency for latency-sensitive tenants
Algorithm defaults: proportional-stepper with derivative dampener enabled to avoid overshoot; credit-bank used only when tenant has burst SLA
Safety default fences chosen conservatively: max_scale 40% per minute, cooldown 120s, minimum_headroom 10%
Telemetry trade-off: emit per-decision payloads but sample to 10% for high-throughput tenants to limit overhead

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Oscillation under high variance workloads. Mitigation: derivative dampener + min_cooldown and sampled decision telemetry to analyze behavior.
Risk: Cost surge if fences mis-configured. Mitigation: default conservative fences and canary budget metering with automatic rollback if spend delta > 25%
Risk: Telemetry overhead at fleet scale. Mitigation: sample decision events and limit payload size; use async emission pipeline
Risk: Tenant SLA conflicts for reserved capacity. Mitigation: tenant-level overrides and an explicit admission-check that prevents Sentinel from violating committed throughput guarantees
